subject: Suncrest inference ops — targets, models, and topology (post-call)
messages:
From: Avery Johnson <avery.johnson@redwood.ai>
To: Sam Park <sam.park@suncrest.ai>, Priya Menon <priya@cloudops.suncrest.ai>
Cc: monica.patel@redwood.ai, grace.oconnor@redwood.ai
Date: 2029-08-30T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Suncrest inference ops — targets, models, and topology (post-call)

Thanks again for the call this morning — great conversation. Short recap and concrete next steps so we all have the same picture. Please flag anything I misremember.

Big picture pain and goals
- Pain: user-facing chat experiences are seeing 95-99th percentile latency spikes during peak hours (noted up to ~1.2s) which hurts retention. Batch scoring (daily jobs) also contends with live traffic and causes throughput degradation.
- Goal: 1) Reduce tail latency to improve UX; 2) guarantee throughput for batch scoring without impacting live traffic; 3) maintain data residency in us-west-2 and HIPAA-aware handling for a subset of datasets.

Quantitative targets discussed (please confirm)
- Live chat SLO: 99th percentile latency < 350 ms for typical requests (avg ~250 tokens), p50 < 75 ms.
- Throughput target: steady-state 400 qps across the chat route; burst capacity to 1,200 qps for scheduled traffic.
- Batch scoring: isolated window for 200k requests/day, peak 2k qps for short windows; acceptable to run on reserved capacity.
- Token profile: avg request ~256 tokens in, 40 tokens out; 95th seq length <= 1024.

Model / quality constraints
- Need an instruction-tuned open model with strong safety filters and deterministic outputs for the assistant flows. Preference for 8-bit quantized mainline model and a smaller 13B low-latency fallback for sub-200ms fast paths.
- Candidate rollout: Redwood-verified "OpenInstruction-70B-8q" as primary and "OpenChat-13B-4q" as low-latency fallback. We will run A/B on a small percent of traffic during PoC.

Topology & ops notes
- Primary region: us-west-2 with dedicated GPU pool (reserved capacity) for chat; autoscale policy with burst quota to a shared pool in us-east-1 as cross-region fallback.
- KV / prefix cache: Redis cluster colocated in the VPC for prefix/KV caching (expected 30% cache hit rate based on your prefix analysis). TTLs ~24h for conversation context caching.
- Routing policy: latency-priority for web routes (route -> 13B fallback if 70B > 350ms), cost-priority for background scoring (can run on larger batch-optimized instances).
- Observability: per-route token cost, per-request latency percentiles, and sampled traces flowing to your Splunk (you mentioned existing stack). Retention: 30 days for traces, 90 days for token-level billing export (can extend).

Security / compliance notes
- VPC peering + KMS integration for model keys; we confirmed Suncrest requires customer-managed keys for Private deployments.

Attachments included: suncrest_poc_requirements.pdf (PoC scoping doc), kv_cache_diagram.png (topology sketch).

Immediate asks / next steps
1) Sam: confirm SLO numbers above and provide expected steady QPS by route (chat vs background) — by EOD Friday (2029-08-30).
2) Priya: security contact and any additional compliance checklists we should run for HIPAA items.
3) Redwood (Monica): will send a one-page PoC plan and a rough capacity estimate for the two-model strategy by Monday.
4) Agree on a 60–90 minute deep-dive with infra + SRE to lock topology and runbook (proposed 2029-09-04).

Thanks — attaching a short PoC proposal next.

– Avery
Avery Johnson

Thanks, Avery — this matches our notes closely. A few clarifications:
- Our 99th percentile numbers are closer to 1.1s at peak (measured last week) — we want to get under 400 ms, ideally under 300 ms after optimizations.
- For batch scoring, the 200k/day figure is accurate; we can move that to an off-peak maintenance window if that simplifies capacity isolation.
- We do require customer-managed KMS and audit logs for the subset of PHI traffic — happy to share the security contact.

Actioning: attaching a small sample of request/response payloads to help with prefix/cache estimates.

Sam
Sam Park
Head of Platform Engineering, Suncrest AI
sam.park@suncrest.ai

From: Avery Johnson <avery.johnson@redwood.ai>

Cc: monica.patel@redwood.ai, grace.oconnor@redwood.ai
Date: 2029-08-31T10:42:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Suncrest inference ops — targets, models, and topology (post-call)

Appreciate the sample, Sam — that's helpful. Monica looped in with a proposed PoC plan below; high level here and a request for a quick capacity estimate from ops:

Proposed PoC (3-week):
- Week 1: Baseline & profiling — replay sample traffic against the OpenInstruction-70B-8q model in a Redwood sandbox (measure 95/99 pctl, token costs, KV hit rates).
- Week 2: Low-latency route test — add OpenChat-13B-4q as a fast fallback and validate fall-through routing, measure end-to-end p99 and p50.
- Week 3: Scale & isolation — run batch scoring jobs during designated windows against reserved capacity and simulate bursts to validate autoscale and fallback policies.

Technical asks for ops estimate (can you provide by Monday):
- Expected concurrent live sessions for chat at steady-state and at peak (per minute or per second).
- Proportion of requests with long prefixes (>=512 tokens).
- Any egress constraints or allowed cross-region failover limits.

Monica will send the PoC doc and a first-pass capacity calc. After that, we can schedule the infra deep-dive (SRE + infra + your cloud team).

Proposed deep-dive: 2029-09-04 10:00 AM PT — does that work?

– Avery
